meanings.note: surprise or indignation: 'Ах ты, ...!' = why, you ...!

examples.text: Ах ты, жадина! А у тебя есть телефон?
examples.trans: Oh, you greedy thing! And have you got a phone?

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
present есть; у меня есть = I have

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

examples.text: Ты мой главный учитель и верный наставник.
examples.trans: You are my main teacher and true mentor.

examples.text: А я вообще очень верная женщина.
examples.trans: And I am actually a very loyal woman.

meanings.note: after a plural noun or pronoun: вы все

examples.text: И знаешь, что самое главное? Всем всё равно.
examples.trans: And you know the main thing? Nobody cares.

examples.text: Решается ваш вопрос, Клавдия Викторовна! Вы не видите, у меня встреча?
examples.trans: Your question is being sorted out, Klavdia Viktorovna! Can't you see I have a meeting?

meanings.note: ends a conversation or an order: 'Всё, свободен' = that's all, you can go
at the start of a sentence

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

выяснить.gloss: to find out, clarify, sort out

examples.trans: Have we sorted all this out?
I'll find everything out right now.

examples.text: Мы выяснили это всё? Можем ехать домой?
examples.trans: Have we sorted all this out? Can we go home?

meanings.note: думать о + prepositional = to think about

examples.trans: I have no time to think about that.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'из мэрии' = from the town hall

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я уже знаю. Мне звонили из мэрии.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I already know. The town hall called me.
There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: мне кажется = I think, it seems to me

examples.trans: I think I've seen you somewhere.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'chef's hat, cap' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The chef wears a white chef's hat.

examples.text: Я съем колпак, если мои повара уйдут!
examples.trans: I will eat my chef's hat if my cooks leave!
I will eat my chef's hat!

meanings.note: in business, sport or an election

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?
Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.en: to lie, to be lying down, to rest

examples.text: Такие люди должны лежать в особенном месте!
examples.trans: Such people should lie in a special place!
The book is lying on the table.
But I'll be lying next to Grishka for eternity.

молчать.gloss: to be silent, to say nothing

meanings.en: to be silent, to keep quiet
meanings.note: почему ты молчишь? = why aren't you saying anything?

examples.text: Ну что ты молчишь? Ты толстый, ты не спортсмен!
examples.trans: Well, why are you so quiet? You're fat, you're no athlete!

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!
The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'стоящий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('real, genuine').

examples.text: Ваня, да пойми ты наконец! Это настоящий успех.
examples.trans: Vanya, understand at last! This is real success.

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'благодарный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('ungrateful').

examples.text: Послушай, не клади трубку! Ах ты, неблагодарная!
examples.trans: Listen, don't hang up! Oh, you ungrateful girl!

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'медленно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
needs 'не' with the verb: никто не войдёт

examples.trans: I know the town like nobody else.

examples.text: Садитесь и держите дверь. Никто не войдёт.
examples.trans: Sit down and hold the door. Nobody will come in.

meanings.note: usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: + prepositional; об before a vowel: об этом

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('careful, cautious').

examples.trans: Be careful, he is very cunning.
I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'варской'). Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('chef's, culinary').

examples.trans: The chef put on a chef's hat.
I will eat my chef's hat!
The chef's hat is lying on the table.
Can I go and have a look?
Why are we going so slowly?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

examples.text: Ничего я тебе не скажу, предатель!
examples.trans: I won't tell you anything, traitor!
Very well! Have a pleasant evening.

meanings.note: document detailing qualifications and work experience

examples.trans: Max showed his résumé to the chef.

examples.text: Я принёс своё резюме для шеф-повара.
examples.trans: I brought my résumé for the head chef.

examples.text: Максим, я внимательно прочла ваше резюме.
examples.trans: Maksim, I carefully read your résumé.

examples.text: Слушай, Нина, это же тот самый ресторан!
examples.trans: Listen, Nina, this is that very restaurant!

examples.text: Мы рады видеть вас в нашем ресторане.
examples.trans: We are glad to see you in our restaurant.
They called from the Italian restaurant.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: formal meeting in which an applicant is evaluated for employment

examples.text: Я пришёл на собеседование в ресторан.
examples.trans: I came for an interview at the restaurant.

examples.text: Завтра у меня важное собеседование на работу.
examples.trans: Tomorrow I have an important job interview.
We will sit together in a friendly way at the table.

examples.text: Не бойся, всё в порядке! Посидим дружно за столом.
examples.trans: Don't be afraid, everything is fine! We will sit together in a friendly way at the table.
Take your feet off the table quickly!

examples.text: Скоро. А пока я есть хочу, слона бы съел!
examples.trans: Soon. But for now I'm hungry, I could eat an elephant!

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'знать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to recognise; to find out', paired with 'узнавать'.

examples.trans: I'll find out where he is.
You recognised me. Thanks for seeing me.

ходить.gloss: to walk, to go (on foot, regularly)

meanings.en: to walk, to go on foot
meanings.note: back and forth or habitually; one trip in one direction: идти

examples.text: Мальчик ходит на костылях. А она ещё и активистка.
examples.trans: The boy walks on crutches. And she's an activist, too.

meanings.note: agrees with the thing owned: чей дом, чья машина, чьё письмо, чьи деньги

examples.text: Курица? Нет. А чей это холодильник?
examples.trans: Chicken? No. And whose fridge is this?

meanings.note: the plural is a different word: люди, людям, о людях

examples.trans: There are a lot of people here.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)

meanings.note: Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'fury, rage' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Шеф будет в ярости, если узнает!
examples.trans: The chef will be furious if he finds out!
It seems the chef is in a real fury.
